card.title: Economics of production; cash flow in the production cycle

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Production economics is a cash loop with lags: capital buys inputs, inputs become product, product becomes revenue, revenue splits into reinvestment, repayment and profit. Costs split into fixed (depreciation, salaries — output-blind) and variable (raw materials, energy — stoichiometry-driven), and break-even output = fixed ÷ contribution per unit.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - Total cost = fixed + variable × output; Revenue = price × output - Break-even output = fixed cost ÷ (price − variable cost per unit)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Covers only: economics of production, cash flow in the production cycle (within Fundamentals of Applied Chemistry).  ·  Out of scope here: topics of neighbouring units in Chemistry — don't mix them.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Three levers run every plant: yield (variable cost), throughput (fixed cost spread), cycle time (working capital).

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The yield dividend*** - every yield percentage point is raw material not wasted; a cheaper route can beat a better catalyst.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Economics of Production: Where the Money Flows A chemical plant is a cash machine with a loop: **capital invested → raw materials, energy, labour purchased → product made → product sold → revenue returns → part reinvested, part repays capital, part is profit.** The economics of production is the study of this loop — its costs, its timing, and the break-even point where revenue first…  ·  ## 2. Theorem Mirror - **Cash-flow cycle:** capital → inputs (raw materials, energy, labour, overheads) → product → sales → revenue → (reinvest + repay + profit) → back to inputs. The cycle has *time lags*: inventory and credit terms delay the return. - **Fixed costs:** independent of output — plant depreciation, salaries, rent, insurance, interest.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Break-even = fixed / (price - variable per unit) - one formula, one substitution, one mark.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: The cost structure picks the plant type: high fixed + low variable is why bulk chemicals run continuously.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Cash-flow cycle: capital -> inputs -> product -> sales -> revenue -> reinvest/repay/profit, with time lags (inventory, credit). Fixed costs: depreciation, salaries, rent, interest - output-independent. Variable: raw materials, energy, packaging - proportional.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Inventory is cash wearing a costume - the cash-flow cycle's lag is financed as working capital.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 3. Deep Conceptual — Why Raw Materials Dominate Chemical Costs - In most chemical processes the **variable cost is 60–80% of total cost, and raw materials are the largest slice** — energy second, labour a distant third in automated plants.…  ·  ## 4. Deep Conceptual — Time Is a Cost: The Cash-Flow Cycle's Lags - Money spent on raw materials today becomes revenue only after processing, storage, delivery, and the customer's payment terms — weeks to months of lag.…  ·  ## 5. Worked Example Types - **Type A — draw and label:** the cash-flow cycle with its lags. - **Type B — fixed vs variable classification:** sort a cost list into the two bins. - **Type C — break-even calculation:** given fixed costs, price, variable cost — find break-even output. - **Type D — economies of scale argument:** why unit cost falls with output.
